title: Inkwell ingest gateway and schema fallback coordinator
creator: Marcus Lin
description: Goal: Build 'Inkwell', a resilient ingest gateway that performs probabilistic schema scoring, lineage annotation, and coordinates an automatic schema-fallback path to preserve customers' console analytics when upstream producers are noisy or schema-evolving. Scope: (1) a streaming pre-processor that scores events against the active contract using a lightweight probabilistic scorer (fast decision path) and tags events with a schema_confidence score; (2) a small nearline repair pipeline (repair.shim) that attempts minimal coercions for low-confidence events and emits repaired copies to the main pipeline; (3) a fallback coordinator which, under sustained contract drift, routes events to a permissive "compat" topic and surfaces a summarized mutation batch to the contract registry for review; (4) operator-facing metrics, traces, and a canary rollout plan. Acceptance criteria: (A) end-to-end ingest latency increase <= 6ms p95 for median event size under normal load; (B) high-confidence pass-through rate >= 95% for stable producers; (C) repaired event accuracy >= 92% on synthetic drift suite; (D) automatic fallback triggers are auditable in Console and reversible via rollout; (E) alerts fire for fallback rate > 0.5% sustained over 10m. Design highlights and trade-offs: - Probabilistic scoring vs full schema validation: we choose a two-tier approach to keep fast-path latency low while still catching regressions. The scorer uses feature hashes (field presence, type fingerprints, enum hits) and a trained logistic regression returned as protobuf for edge evaluation. - Nearline repair: only safe coercions (string->enum mapping via whitelist, number coercions with bounds) are attempted; more invasive repairs are quarantined for human review. - Backpressure: integrate with existing ingest token-bucket and add a soft-shed policy that prioritizes high-confidence events for immediate processing, while buffering low-confidence events to the repair queue. - Observability: add a new per-customer metric series ingest.schema_confidence.p{50,95,99}, fallback.rate, repair.success.rate, and tracing spans for scorer->repair->router. - Security: repair module runs with least privilege and does not send raw payloads to third parties; KMS access for sensitive fields is proxied via platform key service. Migration and rollout plan: 1) Deploy Inkwell scorer behind feature flag for 5% of traffic in staging; 2) Run in 'observe-only' mode for 72h and capture metrics + false-positive/false-negative counts against golden dataset; 3) Enable nearline repairs for canary customers with explicit opt-in; 4) Expand to 25% then 100% with rollback window. Monitoring and runbook: create a Console dashboard with top failing producers, schema_confidence histograms by producer, and a runbook for fallback investigations and manual re-ingestion. Testing: unit tests for scorer determinism, e2e tests with Synthetic Drift Suite, chaos testing to validate fallback under transient Kafka partitions. Open questions: - How to version scorer models across tenants? (per-tenant vs global) proposal: global model with tenant-specific feature biases recorded in metadata. - Threshold tuning strategy: do we allow auto-tune based on rolling false-positive rate or require manual ops approval? Implementation plan: Phase 1 (3 sprints) - scorer library + integration with ingest proxy, metrics hooks. Phase 2 (2 sprints) - nearline repair pipeline and repair APIs. Phase 3 (2 sprints) - fallback coordinator, console UI surfaces, and rollout automation. Backward compatibility: preserve the current ingest schema contract and ensure compat topic subscribers can opt into permissive consumption. Long-term roadmap: couple Inkwell signals into Optimize and Console's Quality Monitoring to trigger model/quantization advice when certain traffic patterns correlate with degraded inference quality.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Marcus Lin: Created initial ticket and uploaded design sketch to Confluence. Marked as P1 because multiple customers saw spikes in repair churn last quarter.
